title: A gate is an interrupt: a request for the operator's sign-off that ends its holder's turn, and nothing more
situation: The operator, 2026-10-16: what sign-off-gates built for the gate is a bug. It detected gates by reading a reply's wording, told the operator apart from the request itself, and kept a gate's content from the party that delegated the work. A gate is a human-in-the-loop interrupt, and holds by construction without any of that.
decision: A gate's holder ends its turn with a request for the operator's sign-off, and that is all a gate is. Whoever receives the request holds no sign-off, so it brings it to the operator; this follows from who holds what. A request passing through the delegating party on its way to the operator is no harm. Nothing detects a gate from a reply's wording, nothing announces a gate apart from the request itself, and nothing shields a gate's content from the delegating party. Joining an agent's session is the harness's own and needs nothing built.
consequences: The gate and operator concepts state this, and attach leaves delivery. Whatever was built to detect, announce or shield a gate is removed, with the known limits recorded against it.
